text: Paulus, apostolus Jesu Christi, ex mandato Dei Servatoris nostri, et Domini Jesu Christi, spei nostrae,
note: *Servātōris* capital: God our Saviour (Θεοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν; decision 20 names *Servātor*), as your settled Eph 5:23, Phil 3:20, John 4:42, Acts 5:31, 13:23 (6 capitals) against Luke 1:47 *dē Deō servātōre meō* (1); so also 2:3 and 4:10 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Timotheo, germano in fide filio, gratiam, misericordiam, pacem a Deo Patre nostro, et Domino Jesu Christo, Domino nostro.
note: *Patre* capital, God the Father (Θεοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν; decision 20), as the greetings of your Gal 1:3, Eph 1:2, 2 Cor 1:2 (*ā Deō Patre nostrō*); *grātiam* stays lower case, the greeting built into the sentence after *Tīmotheō … fīliō,* (1573 *filio, gratiam*, canvas 909) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Scimus sane, bonam esse legem, si quis ea legitime utatur:
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:7 ends a sentence and *Scīmus sānē* turns from the false teachers to the right use of the law (1:8–11), as the NRSV (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Certa res est, et omni approbatione digna, Christum Jesum in mundum venisse servatum sontes, quorum vel primus ego sum.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): the first of the letter's three \"faithful sayings\" (1:15, 3:1, 4:9; Πιστὸς ὁ λόγος), *Certa rēs est* after 1:14's full stop. The saying stands unmarked: Castellio reports it (*Chrīstum Jēsum … vēnisse*, accusative and infinitive), and the BSB has no quotation marks (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Hoc tibi praeceptum commendo, fili Timothee, secundum praegressa de te oracula, ut quemadmodum ea postulant, praeclara fungare militia,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:17's doxology closes with *Āmēn* and *Hoc tibi præceptum commendō, fīlī Tīmothee* turns back to Timothy in direct address, the charge of 1:18–20 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Hoc enim honestum est, nostroque Servatori Deo acceptum,
note: *Servātōrī* capital, God our Saviour (τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Θεοῦ; decision 20), as 1:1 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: suam domum bene administrans, liberos habens dicto audientes, summa cum gravitate.
note: *administrāns,* with a comma, as 1573 (*ſuam domum bene adminiſtrans , liberos habens*, canvas 910): two participles, not one phrase; *suam* lower case, the list of 3:2–3 running on (written here, as a layout line stops the pipeline's own lowering) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quod si quis suam ipsius domum administrare nescit, quo pacto Dei ecclesiam procurabit?
note: *prōcūrābit?* with 1573's question mark (*quo pacto Dei eccleſiam procurabit ?*, canvas 910; πῶς … ἐπιμελήσεται;) for the draft's full stop (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: ut, si tardem, scias, quomodo sit in Dei domo versandum, quae est Dei viventis ecclesia, veritatis columen atque firmamentum.
note: *ecclēsia,* with 1573's comma (*Dei viuentis eccleſia , veritatis columen*, canvas 910): *vēritātis columen atque firmāmentum* is in apposition (στῦλος καὶ ἑδραίωμα τῆς ἀληθείας), not a genitive on *ecclēsia*; *ut* lower case, 3:14 ends with a comma (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Et profecto magnum est pietatis arcanum: \\q1 Deus apparuit in carne, \\q2 per Spiritum commendatus est, \\q1 conspectus angelis, \\q2 praedicatus gentibus, \\q1 creditus in mundo, \\q2 receptus in gloria.
note: the hymn after *magnum est pietātis arcānum:* as poetry in six lines, as the BSB sets it (its *b q1 q2 …*), mid-verse as your 2 Cor 8:15; a hymn of the church, not Scripture, so no \\qt and no marks, as your Phil 2:6–11 and Rom 11:33–36; *Deus* keeps its capital (the TR's Θεός). *Spīritum* keeps the draft's capital (ἐν πνεύματι, BSB \"by the Spirit\"; the NRSV \"in spirit\", 1573 *per ſpiritum*): uncertain. Chapter 4's paragraph closes the poetry (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nam ideo et laboramus, et probra patimur, quod spem habemus in vivente Deo, qui quum omnium, tum maxime fidentium hominum Servator est.
note: *Servātor* capital, God (ὅς ἐστι σωτὴρ πάντων ἀνθρώπων; decision 20), a predicate as your settled Eph 5:23 *corporis Servātor est*; *Nam* keeps its capital after 4:9's colon, as your settled books after a colon (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Effice, ut nemo tuam iuventutem despiciat: quin fidentibus exemplo esto, verbis, moribus, caritate, spiritu, fide, castitate.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 4:11 *Hæc præcipitō ac docētō.* closes the instructions to teach, and *Effice, ut nēmō tuam juventūtem dēspiciat* turns to Timothy's own example (4:12–16); *estō,* with 1573's comma (*exemplo eſto , verbis*, canvas 910), the list naming where he is to be an example; *spīritū* lower case, his own spirit (ἐν πνεύματι, TR) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Vidua cooptetur non minor annis sexaginta, quae unius viri fuerit uxor,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 5:8 ends a sentence and *Vidua cooptētur* opens a new step, the roll of widows and who is to be enrolled (5:9–10), set against the younger widows of 5:11 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Aiunt enim litterae: \\qt “Bovi trituranti os ne obturato,”\\qt* et \\qt “Dignus est operarius mercede sua.”\\qt*
note: two quotations after *Ajunt enim litteræ:* (λέγει γὰρ ἡ γραφή), as the BSB: Deut 25:4 (as your 1 Cor 9:9 *\\qt “Bovī trītūrantī ōs nē obstruitō.”\\qt**) and the saying of Luke 10:7 (your *dignus est operārius mercēde suā*), each in \\qt with “…”, prose, *et* (καί) between them outside the marks; *Bovī* and *Dignus* capital, each a quotation's first word (1573 *& , Dignus*, canvas 911); *obtūrātō,”* with a comma inside for the draft's colon, closing the first quotation (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Nonnullorum hominum peccata perspicua sunt, et judicium anteveniunt: in nonnullis vero subsequuntur.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break; it breaks at 5:23 too, taken here only once): after the personal counsel of 5:23 on wine, *Nōnnūllōrum hominum peccāta perspicua sunt* returns to the judging of men (5:24–25), the matter of 5:22 *Manūs nēminī prōtinus impōnitō* (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Edico tibi in Dei conspectu, vitam dantis omnibus, itemque Christi Jesu, qui coram Pontio Pilato praeclara illa confessione verum testatus est,
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 6:12 ends a sentence and *Ēdīcō tibi in Deī cōnspectū* opens the solemn charge (6:13–16) that closes in the doxology (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Quam profitentes quidam a fide aberrarunt. Adsit tibi gratia: Amen. \\cls Scripta est Laodiceae, quae Pacatianae Phrygiae caput est.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as your 2 Cor 13:14 and Gal 6:18, as 1573 prints it apart under the blessing (*Scripta eſt Laodiceæ, quæ Pacatianæ Phrygiæ caput eſt.*, canvas 912), with its full stop (the draft has none); *grātia: Āmēn.* keeps 1573's colon (*gratia : Amen .*) (Claude, 2026-11-11)
